thread:
maria: Heads up — ran a quick nsys pass on q2 load (seq len 2048, batch=4) and I'm seeing a weird cluster of 1-2ms spikes between kernel selection and kv_prefetch. attaching perf timeline later but wanted to get thoughts on NVTX ranges/naming before I instrument further

anika: can you paste the short timeline? curious if it's the admission window or kv cache miss path

maria: gist of trace (condensed):
```
--- timeline snippet ---
0.001s  NVTX: request_start
0.002s  NVTX: route:kernel-selector
0.004s  kernel_launch: matmul_fused
0.006s  NVTX: kv_prefetch
0.007s  kernel_launch: kv_load
0.009s  NVTX: per-request-cache-check
0.010s kernel_launch: matmul_fused (fallback)
```
---
Looks like NVTX ranges are too coarse — route:kernel-selector encloses multiple small decisions. when we collapse everything into one range we lose which branch caused the 1-2ms hop.

liam: ugh. that's the classic "selector spans too fat" problem. i'd suggest two things: (1) add a shallow per-request decision span (name it e.g. `selector:choice`) for each branch, (2) keep kv-prefetch out as its own fine-grain range so we can correlate prefetch latency with actual kernel launches

anika: agree. naming conv proposal: top-level `req:<id>`, decision-level `req:<id>/selector:<policy>` and kernel ranges `req:<id>/kernel:<name>[:variant]`. for kv stuff: `req:<id>/kv:check` and `req:<id>/kv:prefetch`

maria: that naming looks good. two followups: how verbose do we want per-token/kv checks? if every token emits `kv:check` we'll drown traces. maybe sample 1% or only on misses

liam: sample yes. also add a density flag so we can enable full verbosity for a single request: `NVTX_PUSH("req:1234|v=full")`

perf-bot: perf-ci results for that nsys job: p50 latency 7.8ms -> 8.4ms after last change (+7.7%). Hotspots: 1) selector decision (variable), 2) kv_prefetch miss path, 3) kernel_launch overhead on fallback variant

maria: interesting — perf-ci correlates with local runs. I think we need both better NVTX granularity and a lightweight telemetry counter for "selector path chosen". then we can aggregate without shipping full traces for every request

anika: for lightweight telemetry, we can increment a per-request stat via our trace counters: `trace_counter.increment("selector.choice.<policy>")` — that will be cheap and show distribution in console

liam: on the instrumentation side, small code snippet i used in a patch that worked well for us (psuedocode):
```
void instrument_selector(Request &r) {
  NVTX_PUSH_FMT("req:%s/selector:%s", r.id, r.policy);
  auto choice = decide_kernel(r);
  NVTX_POP();
  NVTX_PUSH_FMT("req:%s/kernel:%s", r.id, choice.name);
  launch(choice);
  NVTX_POP();
}
```
Couple notes: keep the push/pop symmetric, and avoid long-lived string allocations in hot path (use preallocated small buffers)

maria: good call. i'll prototype with sampling + the `req:<id>/selector` split. if this surfaces a specific policy that's spiking we can add micro-ranges inside that policy (e.g., `selector:policyX/score_calc`)

perf-bot: suggestion from perf-run: try enabling `--nvtx-level=micro` in a local nsys run (there's an env flag in our harness) to validate without full prod-scale sampling

maria: perfect. i'll land a small change behind a feature flag: `runtime.trace.selector_micro=true`. plan: enable on canary, run nsys with `--nvtx-level=micro` for 5k requests, analyze aggregated selector.choice counters, and follow up with a small PR to add `kv:prefetch` range only on misses.

anika: +1. if you tag the trace artifact in the PR (link it) we'll review kernel attribution mapping rules too.

liam: also ping me when you have the canary — happy to correlate perf snapshots and kernel timelines

maria: thanks all — will update when I have the nsys output uploaded (link will go to #eng-runtime-uploads). :rocket:
